changes: Use a shared, exact UTF-16 mapping between native textarea API values and unchanged source candidates; handle LF, CRLF, CR and mixed newlines without migrating records.
Fix evidence navigation, retain-to-cursor and partial rewrite so visible selections address the intended source range, including emoji and multiline text.
Bind delayed selection actions to their record/view; reject mismatched text, invalid bounds, half-CRLF and split-surrogate ranges.
Use the same mapping for literary-scoring source selections; keep preview local and clear a collapsed selection instead of reusing an old passage.
Normalize incoming replacement line breaks only inside explicit author adoption, then preserve the original document EOL and UTF-8 BOM; retain raw candidate provenance and the pre-adoption snapshot.
Initialize existing Diff readiness from the real editor and compare logical newline representations; adopted receipts still require explicit author acceptance and matching content.
Keep existing mixed-source write guards, original revision checks, Diff confirmation and Canon/State boundaries.
Local Preview: real browser/local services and fixed MOCK writer checks are separate from remote AI and native GUI/IME/DPI acceptance.
runtime_validation: Preview / PARTIAL: see the current delivery evidence; headless browser, local checks, real Codex/MCP and packaged workers are separate gates. No native GUI/IME/DPI acceptance is claimed.
features: Character assistants, Python SDK and Codex MCP reuse one typed Action Registry and existing domain services.
On-demand Python Control uses genuine CPython WASI in a bounded owned subprocess, without host project mounts, network or shell.
Real frontend receipts support chapter navigation, pinned references, layouts and actual editor state.
Project/persona-scoped scripts, output history, AI task provenance and explicit read-only result handoffs.
Existing Codex login, concrete models and supported effort/context controls; real task events, result reading, cancellation and supported live steering.
Frozen author confirmations remain valid after a model or Python turn ends; scripts are never automatically replayed.
Source and binary candidates exclude private manuscripts, credentials, conversation history and character assets.
Preview: the action catalog covers designated workflows, not every application operation; new controls primarily support Chinese and English.
